Back in 2012, I took a trip to Arizona to visit a relative.

My relative lives near Phoenix, in a small gated community.

My first reaction was how hot it was. I expected it to be hot, but it was nearly stifling. Thankfully, I'd packed well for the trip.

Where I live in NJ, we have grass and trees in front of our houses. In my relative's part of AZ, they have cacti. [Big cacti](http://i.imgur.com/MX4fEmm.jpg).

My father and I settled into her house and stayed for a day or so, exploring the area, checking out the Native American casinos and the local stores. One thing we found interesting, and saddening, was that they did not have a real pizzeria nearby! We have five or six in my town alone in NJ, but all her community had was a lowly Papa John's. It's funny, the small things you notice when traveling.

Another interesting thing was Arizona's gun laws, and how they differ from our own. [This sign](http://i.imgur.com/FFXqVSm.jpg) was found on one of the local stores. In NJ, it's impossible to get a carry permit. Needless to say, I was surprised to see it.

After spending time with our loved one, we decided to hit the road and head out to Sedona, which was about 4 hours away. And therein lies one of the greatest things about Arizona - [the roads are open](http://i.imgur.com/ybCcUpD.jpg) and the speed limits are high.

We drove for hours through the desert, flying by rock formations and cacti and little shops set up by local Native Americans. Eventually, we arrived in Sedona.

Sedona is an interesting town, situated in the Sonoran desert. It reminded me of a modern wild west town. There were saloon type places, and Western-type shops. We checked into a motel then went back out to explore.

Eventually, we ended up on a desert tour.

The Sonoran desert smells like Juniper. It's a beautiful smell, for [a beautiful place](http://i.imgur.com/OYQQiMs.jpg). Even with the sun beating down on us, it was hard not to be stunned by the [beauty of it](http://i.imgur.com/O7UP4RY.jpg).

Even [the flatter areas](http://i.imgur.com/kK7FzSA.jpg) were interesting, if only because of the [plant life living there](http://i.imgur.com/4XEIfCd.jpg).

After a few hours in the desert we returned to town for a meal. Another thing that differed from NJ is that the restaurants and bars there close quite early - by 8pm! We are used to having access to things 24/7, so being kicked out of a bar at 8 was odd. Dad and I had a few scotchs then made our way to Airport Road. There, we watched the sun set over the desert. It had been on my bucket list. [I was not able to get a great photo - it was much prettier in real life](http://i.imgur.com/VfvN9a8.jpg).

One final thing about AZ that I liked was how they sort of embraced the stereotype of their state, even going so far as to sell [candy with scorpions in it](http://i.imgur.com/R7Sfq8e.jpg). Neat, but no thanks!

We ultimately traveled onward towards the Grand Canyon. I'll post a photo of that sometime. This story was more interesting.
